items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: But we first started with Piku playing Clown and Poison.

ctx.x: That time, with that band, was what Rick Howe was playing, Poison. And sometimes we had Piku with us. Yeah. Yeah. Mostly. Then we'd try to get Willie, but Willie was working with Paul Barber and sometimes with Fredrick Coleman, that. And the same block by Sid DeVille at Montegral. But we first started with Piku playing Clown and Poison. And we had a trombone player by the name of, he died not long ago. That man live uptown there. Not Piers? No, not late. What's his name?

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Because Pickle would make with that tune. Yeah. That was Pickle's tune.

ctx.x: But it was, let's see, the shows used to come in once a week.

Like some shows, it was last two weeks, some of them last one of the vaultables. They played all for the vaultables. They played all for the vaultables shows. And then they had, I think it was, let's see, some of them, I know they use high society a lot. Oh yeah, yeah. They use for the overture. Yeah. High society. High society. Yeah. Because Pickle would make with that tune. Yeah. That was Pickle's tune. Yeah. They had a fellow by the name of, he's a trombone player by the name of, that man's name again,
